The repo uses pytest through two Makefile targets. First install the dev dependencies with `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then:

- **`make test-fast`** runs `pytest -m "not postgres" -q`. It skips the Postgres integration tests and is the one to use day to day.
- **`make test`** runs `pytest -q`, which is the full suite including the Postgres tests.

I haven't run either command; this comes from reading the `Makefile` and `pyproject.toml`.

**A stored note doesn't match the repo.** The team's EngramDB memory says to run `docker compose up db` before `make test` so the Postgres tests can connect. But:
- The repo has no `docker-compose.yml` or `compose.yaml`, so that command won't work here.
- Neither test file (`tests/test_payments.py`, `tests/test_tax.py`) uses the `postgres` marker, and `pyproject.toml` doesn't register it. Right now both targets most likely run the same tests.

The database setup may have been removed, or it may live somewhere else. I've marked that memory as "challenged" so someone can review it. If you know how the Postgres database is supposed to be started, tell me and I'll update the note.
